open_points.subject: Customer erasure revision and last-changed instant
open_points.text: Each action that moves a record's last-changed instant — for a project a correction and archiving (M01); for a Customer a correction, restricting and lifting, ending and resuming the relationship, and erasure (M04) — moves the record's revision by exactly one and sets its last-changed instant to the current instant
open_points.question: When Customer erasure is accepted, does it create a next revision and retain a last-changed instant, or does it leave no revision and no other Customer facts beyond the identity and erased mark, as A04 rule 1, A04-4 and M04 require?
options: Remove Customer erasure from this A04-3 test and test instead that accepted erasure removes the revision and last-changed instant under A04-4.
Retain a next revision and last-changed instant after erasure, which requires reopening A04 rule 1, A04-4, M04 and the earlier requirement that an erased Customer keeps nothing else.
open_points.default_guess: Remove Customer erasure from the actions expected to move and retain the pair, and assert its removal under A04-4.

witness.initial: A Customer has revision 7, a last-changed instant and unerased personal data.
events: The owner submits an erasure stating revision 7, and Registry accepts it.
outcomes: Following Required test 11 literally, the erased Customer has revision 8 and its last-changed instant is set to the current instant.
Following A04 rule 1, A04-4 and M04, the erased Customer has no revision and retains no last-changed instant.
witness.observer: The owner reading the erased Customer sees whether the revision and last-changed instant survived.

open_points.subject: clock readings for record-changing operations
open_points.text: sets its last-changed instant to the current instant
open_points.question: How many UTC wall-clock readings does one atomic mutating operation take when it writes several fresh instants, and must its last-changed, lifecycle and audit instants be the same value?
options: Take one UTC wall-clock reading for the operation and use it for every instant the operation writes.
Take a separate UTC wall-clock reading for each written instant.
Take readings at specified phases of the operation, with an explicit equality or ordering guarantee.
open_points.default_guess: Take one UTC wall-clock reading after admission and use it for every timestamp written by the atomic operation.

witness.initial: An active project has revision 4, and the wall clock advances between successive reads.
events: The operation writes the project's last-changed instant, archived instant and audit-entry instant.
outcomes: An implementation samples the UTC clock once, so all three instants are equal.
An implementation samples for each write, so the three observable instants may differ.
witness.observer: The owner comparing the project card with its audit entry sees the difference.

open_points.subject: security review after the changed A04 decision
open_points.text: A change to a decision a category names reopens this review.
open_points.question: What is the security-review result after this latest A04 change, particularly for the authorization and concurrency categories that reference A04?
options: Re-perform the affected category reviews and record that their outcomes and references remain unchanged.
Re-perform them and record the changed outcomes, references or guarantees that the review finds.
Leave the review reopened, in which case A21 cannot yet claim a completed accepted review.
open_points.default_guess: First resolve A04's erasure contradiction, then re-perform and record the authorization and concurrency reviews; do not silently carry forward the previous result.
